note: Runs the remaining items from the evidence-relation audit (the Sonnet pass recorded in 0143): one pre-existing fail-open in the merged edge code, and three hardening items on the new evidence surface. All draft; each carries a regression test. Files: nestor/decision.py (fail-closed endpoint check), nestor/sqlite_store.py + storage.py + evidence.py + cli.py (domain scope on the report), nestor/portable.py (export warning), nestor/evidence.py (ledger content hash).

decisions.question: The edge endpoint-existence check defaulted memory_get to a lambda returning True, so on a store lacking memory_get a signed edge could be sealed against ids that name no decision. How is that closed?
decisions.commitment: propose_edge and seal_edge now call a _require_pair_lookup() helper that refuses (RuntimeError naming the missing capability) when memory_get is absent, then read the store directly. Fail closed: an edge whose endpoints cannot be verified is one that must not be ratified. A regression test wraps a store to hide memory_get, presents a VALID signature, and asserts seal_edge raises and nothing is sealed.
decisions.why: This revises 0141's 'gracefully skipped on a store without it'. Graceful-skip was defensible for a draft (propose_edge writes an unsigned edge nothing traverses as fact), but on the SIGNED path it let a valid key ratify a relation between decisions that do not exist -- the audit reproduced it. The covenant risk is specifically ratification, so the endpoint check must fail closed exactly where a signature is involved, and applying it to both paths keeps the two consistent. The shipped SqliteStore always has memory_get, so no real deployment loses function; only a hypothetical edge-only store is refused, which is correct.
decisions.doors_closed: Fail-open on the signed edge path (a signature over ghost ids sealing a junk edge). The 'gracefully skipped' wording of 0141 for the seal path (revised).

decisions.question: The unevidenced-seals report had no domain predicate, so a multi-domain store's curator saw decision, translation, and entity seals interleaved with no way to narrow. Intended?
decisions.commitment: No -- it fell out of the query. memory_unevidenced_seals now takes optional source_lang/target_lang (empty = every domain, unchanged default), threaded through evidence.unevidenced_seals and a `nestor evidence report --from/--to`. A test seals a decision-domain and an es/en pair and asserts the unscoped report lists both while each scoped call lists only its own.
decisions.why: Every other domain-scoped surface takes --from/--to; the report silently did not, which reads as an oversight rather than a decision. Making the filter optional keeps the store-wide default (evidence is a pair-level concept, so a whole-store queue is the right default) while giving a multi-domain curator the scoping the rest of the CLI already offers. Cheap, additive, no behaviour change for the unscoped caller.
decisions.doors_closed: A report that can only ever be store-wide (a multi-domain curator could not narrow it).

decisions.question: Bundle export carries no evidence (0143's named follow-up). Silent drop, or visible?
decisions.commitment: Visible. export_bundle now warns (RuntimeWarning) when an exported pair actually has a reference attached, saying evidence is not carried and will be absent after import. It does NOT warn when the store has the capability but no evidence, so there is no false alarm. A test attaches a reference and asserts the warning; the omission itself stays a real follow-up (carrying evidence in the bundle), not fixed here.
decisions.why: Dropping a human-or-machine-recorded reference with no signal is the silent-omission failure the export path already guards against for rejections (supports_rejection_listing warns on the same class of gap). Matching that posture makes the gap honest without pretending it is closed. Warning only when evidence is present keeps the signal meaningful rather than firing on every export from an evidence-capable store.
decisions.doors_closed: Silently exporting a bundle that looks complete while dropping evidence. Claiming the bundle carries evidence (it still does not).

decisions.question: The attach_evidence ledger entry recorded only ids and labels, so an out-of-band edit to a row's locator or reason left no trace. What is added?
decisions.commitment: A content_sha over (kind, locator, reason) is written into the attach_evidence ledger entry, mirroring a seal's source_sha/target_sha. Not a signature -- evidence holds no authority -- but tamper-evidence: a later audit can recompute the hash from the row and detect a mismatch against the append-only chain. A test asserts the entry's content_sha equals the expected digest.
decisions.why: The ledger is the tamper-evident record; an entry that names a row but does not fix its content lets the row drift from what was recorded without the chain noticing. A seal already records content hashes for exactly this; evidence carrying one gives audit-completeness parity at negligible cost, while staying honest that it is evidence-of-tampering, not a barrier to it (which would need a signature evidence deliberately does not have).
decisions.doors_closed: A ledger entry that cannot detect a later edit to the evidence row's content. Confusing tamper-evidence with authority (content_sha is not a signature and confers nothing).
